title: 2013 Using Zone Entry Data To Separate Offensive, Neutral, And Defensive Zone Performance
file_name: 2013 Using Zone Entry Data To Separate Offensive, Neutral, And Defensive Zone Performance.pdf
universal_lens: The fundamental unification maps discrete zone transitions to a stochastic renewal process. By normalizing event generation (shots/goals) against the rate of boundary crossings, we isolate intrinsic state-space efficiency from raw temporal exposure, decoupling possession-driven volume from true per-visit performance metrics.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs conformal inference on the empirical distribution of shots-per-entry. We treat observed entries as exchangeable sequences, calculating conformance scores for out-of-distribution neutral zone carries versus dumps, yielding rigorous prediction intervals for future shot differentials without relying on parametric priors.
gse_mapping: GSE models ice time as a continuous-time Markov chain with absorbing states at the blue lines. The operator tracks expected value gradients across the neutral zone, dynamically updating transition probabilities based on real-time puck-carry success rates and defensive suppression coefficients.

primitives.assumptions: Offensive and defensive zone performances are statistically stationary and exhibit low variance between players compared to neutral zone transitions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails during extreme tactical deviations, such as prolonged penalty kill scenarios where neutral zone transit is bypassed.

layer2.telemetry: Net entries with possession minus opponent entries with possession.

primitives.name: Carry vs Dump Gradient
primitives.verbatim_quote: Neutral zone success involves more than getting extra zone entries; since carrying the puck across the blue line generates more than twice as many shots, scoring chances, and goals as dumping the puck in, gaining the zone with possession is a major driver of success.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Shots/Goals: dimensionless count; Carry/Dump: categorical boolean state of entry method.
primitives.assumptions: The causal link between entry method and subsequent shot generation is invariant across different defensive matchups.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if opposing teams employ trap defenses that completely neutralize the advantage of entering with possession.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's feature weighting matrix, assigning higher prior weights to controlled entries in predictive win-probability models.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of shots generated following a carry-in versus a dump-in.

reasoning_traces.think:
Traditional hockey analytics suffer from severe confounding variables: a player's defensive metric (shots allowed) is artificially inflated or deflated by their teammate's offensive possession generation. To mathematically resolve this duality, we must abandon time-based denominators (per game/per minute) and adopt an event-based denominator (per possession). The foundational operator here is the Possession-Normalized Efficiency. By defining a 'possession' strictly via the physical crossing of the blue line (zone entry), we establish a discrete renewal process. Each entry resets the state space, allowing us to calculate the expected yield of shots or goals per visit. However, simply counting entries is insufficient. The data reveals a profound isomorphism between the neutral zone and ultimate shot differential. The neutral zone acts as the primary filter or bottleneck for generating high-quality possessions. This introduces the Carry vs Dump Gradient. Mathematically, the state of the system upon entering the offensive zone—puck possessed versus puck dumped—creates two distinct probability distributions for subsequent shot generation. The carry state yields a significantly higher mean shot production. Therefore, the true sovereign primitive is not merely the offensive zone performance, but the neutral zone's ability to force the system into the high-yield 'carry' state. Failure modes emerge when sample sizes of entries are too small, causing the efficiency ratios to diverge wildly, or when extreme defensive systems (like the trap) collapse the gradient between carrying and dumping, rendering the entry method statistically indistinguishable in outcome.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This methodology traces its lineage to early 20th-century queuing theory and renewal processes, specifically the shift from time-average to ensemble-average measurements. It mirrors the evolution of baseball analytics from batting average (hits per at-bat) to weighted runs created, acknowledging that not all events (entries) are created equal. The explicit tracking of boundary crossings echoes the development of spatial statistics in epidemiology, where infection rates are normalized by contact events rather than population time.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling the opposing agent requires recognizing that coaches actively manipulate these primitives. A coach deploying a defensive pair against elite opponents is attempting to force the opposing system into the low-yield 'dump' state or prevent entries entirely. The decision actor (coach/player) operates under bounded rationality, trading off immediate possession security (dumping) against long-term expected value (carrying). Our mathematical framework must account for this adversarial optimization, treating the neutral zone not as empty space, but as a contested probabilistic battlefield where agents dynamically adjust their transition matrices to maximize their own shot differential while minimizing the opponent's.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: We must veto any analytical layer that attempts to re-introduce raw time-on-ice as a primary scaling factor for per-possession metrics, as this reintroduces the exact confounding variable we sought to eliminate. Furthermore, we veto the assumption that all zone entries are equally valuable regardless of score context or game situation; a late-game entry while trailing carries a vastly different utility function than a first-period entry. Leakage occurs if we fail to properly isolate even-strength situations, as power-play dynamics fundamentally alter the geometry and probability distributions of zone entries, collapsing the neutral zone dominance kernel into a purely numerical advantage primitive.
